name: isAdminMFAPhishingResistant
definition: CONTESTED -- no single meaning is held: six integrations answer this key with five incompatible truth conditions (a phishing-resistant factor is merely available, the whole org permits only phishing-resistant factors, every admin has one enrolled, every admin sign-in is required to use one, or one admin policy permits one), listed under conflict.positions; until the owner rules, no new implementation may be added under this name.
population: unknown -- differs per position: the org-wide factor catalogue (not admins), users holding an admin role, or the vendor's own admin-console sign-in policy
evidenceRequiredForTrue: unknown -- the five positions require five different reads, and they also disagree on which methods count as phishing-resistant; see conflict.positions

conflict.summary: All emitters agree on the TYPE (boolean) and disagree on what true asserts and on what counts as phishing-resistant. Five meanings: availability (some phishing-resistant factor is ACTIVE in the org); org-wide restriction (only phishing-resistant factors are ACTIVE, which entails admins); admin enrollment coverage (every admin has an ACTIVE phishing-resistant authenticator enrolled, phishable ones may coexist); admin enforcement (every admin sign-in is required to use a phishing-resistant method); and one-policy permission (an admin-console policy requires MFA and lists WebAuthn among the factors it allows). The phishing-resistant sets also differ: WebAuthn and FIDO U2F only (Okta pin); WebAuthn, U2F, Okta FastPass and smart card (Okta main); FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business and multi-factor certificate (Azure AD); WebAuthn only (Duo, JumpCloud); passkeys and security keys only (Google); FIDO2 or Microsoft Authenticator (an unwired file). Okta's main file holds two of these meanings itself, chosen by which body the definition hands it.

positions.meaning: Availability -- at least one phishing-resistant factor type (webauthn, or token:hardware from provider FIDO) is ACTIVE in the org's factor catalogue. Phishable factors active beside it are ignored; admins are not read.
positions.population: the org factor catalogue (GET /api/v1/org/factors), not administrators
positions.source: Pinned file read for this entry: PHISH_RESISTANT_TYPES = ["webauthn"], PHISH_RESISTANT_COMBOS = [("token:hardware", "FIDO")], verdict has_phish_resistant = len(active_phish_resistant) > 0. QC 2026-10-06 F-iam-mfa-02: passes an org whose admins can still use SMS; an empty list returns False with dataCollection success.

positions.meaning: Org-wide restriction -- phishing-resistant factors (webauthn, u2f, signed_nonce/FastPass, smart_card) are ACTIVE and no phishable factor is, so every member including admins can authenticate only with them; false when none is ACTIVE; not evaluated when both kinds are ACTIVE.
positions.population: the org factor catalogue (GET /api/v1/org/factors), not administrators; per-admin reads, when merged, only name accounts and never change the verdict

positions.meaning: Admin enrollment coverage -- every user holding an Okta admin role has an ACTIVE phishing-resistant authenticator enrollment (webauthn, smart_card_idp, okta_verify_fastpass); false when any admin's ACTIVE enrollments are all known-phishable; not evaluated on indeterminate, inactive or partial reads. An admin with FIDO2 and SMS both enrolled counts as covered.
positions.population: users holding an Okta admin role (GET /api/v1/iam/assignees/users) and their authenticator enrollments

positions.meaning: Admin enforcement -- every administrator sign-in is required to use a phishing-resistant method: Azure AD by enabled Conditional Access requiring an authentication strength of only fido2, windowsHelloForBusiness or x509CertificateMultiFactor for every admin role in Microsoft's template (or all users); Google by 2-Step Verification enforced for every active super or delegated admin and every factor policy PASSKEY_ONLY; Duo by the Admin Panel login setting permitting WebAuthn and nothing phishable.
positions.population: administrators of the identity platform: Entra admin-role holders, Google super and delegated admins, Duo Admin Panel administrators
positions.source: Code read for this entry: Azure from_ca_policies :335-408 (True only from CA; False from email OTP enabled :213-223 or AdminMFAV2 below 100% :429-436); Google :187-222; Duo :300-333. QC F-iam-mfa (Entra 'three bodies, each answering only what it can prove').

positions.meaning: One-policy permission -- at least one enabled JumpCloud authentication policy scoped to the Admin Portal requires MFA and lists WEBAUTHN among its allowed factors; other, phishable factors may be allowed beside it.
positions.population: JumpCloud authentication policies scoped to admin_portal
positions.source: Code read for this entry: has_phishing_resistant = any(t in PHISHING_RESISTANT_FACTORS for t in types) :172-176 -- any, not all. An empty policy list returns False with dataCollection success.

decision.question: Does isAdminMFAPhishingResistant assert that every admin sign-in is REQUIRED to use a phishing-resistant method (Azure AD, Google, Duo), that every admin HAS one enrolled (Okta coverage path), or that the org permits only phishing-resistant factors (Okta factor-list path) -- and which methods count (is Okta FastPass in, are smart card and certificate in)? The availability (Okta - Application pin) and one-policy (JumpCloud) positions pass tenants whose admins can still use phishable factors.
